title: Enlisted Aviation Logistician (MGySgt to GySgt) NMOS (6019, 6042, 6391, 6591, 6672), DC AVN
raw_text:
2. MOS 6617, Enlisted Aviation Logistician (MGySgt to GySgt) NMOS (6019,
6042, 6391, 6591, 6672), DC AVN

    a. Summary. Aviation Logisticians are assigned to selected headquarters
and staffs. They are trained in aviation logistics (AVLOG) support plan
development. The skill set provides headquarters staffs with aviation
logistics specific subject matter expertise to support the force deployment
planning and execution process, exercise planning, pre-positioning program
development and execution, and doctrine development.

       b.    Prerequisites

             (1) Security requirement:   secret security clearance eligibility.

        (2) Must possess MOS 6019, Aircraft Maintenance Chief; MOS 6042,
Individual Material Readiness List (IMRL) Asset Manager, MOS 6391, Avionics
Chief, MOS 6591, Aviation Ordnance Chief, or MOS 6672, Aviation Supply
Specialist.

       c.    Requirements

             (1) Complete at least two of the following courses:

             (a) Maritime Prepositioning Force (MPF) Staff Planning Course,
covered by the Expeditionary Warfare Training Group (K-2E-3119) or (N03L8Q1
or N30L8Q1).

            (b) Joint Logistics Course (JLC) (A14L232) at the U.S. Army
Logistics University (ALU), Ft Gregg-Adams, VA.



                                          3-430                        Enclosure (1)
 3144                                                               NAVMC 1200.1L



            (c) Joint Operations Planning and Execution System (JOPES) Action
Officer Course (JAOC) (JD2101) at Ft Eustis, VA.

            (d) Joint Operations Planning and Execution System (JOPES)
Support Personnel Course (JSPC) (JD1102) at Ft Eustis, VA.

       d.   Duties

        (1) Serve as AVLOG representative for operational planning teams
(OPT) and crisis action teams (CAT).

        (2) Support the development, review, and update of OPLANS/CONPLANS in
support of higher headquarters directives.

        (3) Review/validate time phased force deployment data to ensure
compliance with guidance and directives.

            (4) Develop estimates of supportability and concepts of logistics
support.

        (5) Support the development and operational orders and letters of
instruction for ACE operations and exercises.

       e.   Related Standard Occupational Classification (SOC) Title and Code

            (1) General and Operations Managers 11-1021.

            (2) Administrative Services Managers 11-3011.

            (3) Transportation, Storage, and Distribution Managers 11-3071.

            (4) Logisticians 13-1081.

            (5) Operations Research Analysts 15-2031.

       f.   Related Military Skill.     None.
common_text: The Aviation Logistics OccFld includes personnel in the areas of aviation supply, aviation information systems, and aviation logistics planning. Qualifications required include operating various information technology systems, understanding and utilizing related publications, possessing distinct communicative and writing skills, and the ability to work independently and closely with additional logistical functional areas. The duties involve administration and operational procedures, office and warehouse management procedures, preparation and use of military publications and the preparation of accounting documents. Formal schooling is provided to Marines entering the Aviation Supply Specialist and Aviation Information Systems Specialist MOSs. Types of entry-level jobs include work as aviation supply logistics and AIS. There are a wide variety of billets available in the OccFld ranging from duty at all levels of the Marine Aircraft Wing/Marine Aviation Logistics Squadron to various Non-FMF billets such as HMX-1 and instructor duty. Aviation Logisticians are primarily aviation supply, aviation maintenance, aviation ordnance, and avionics personnel on higher headquarters staffs that coordinate/conduct aviation logistics planning in support of OPLANS/CONPLANS. In addition to a thorough understanding of their primary MOS, these personnel are involved with the Marine Aviation Logistics Support Program (MALSP), the Marine Corps Planning Process, the Joint operations Planning and Execution System (JOPES), Maritime Prepositioning Force (MPF) operations, and employment of the aviation logistics ship (TAVB). The Aviation Logistics OccFld has been expanded to include principal responsibility in the management and execution of CNO and CMC-directed strategies for continuous process improvement.

body:
The Aviation Logistics OccFld includes personnel in the areas of aviation supply, aviation information systems, and aviation logistics planning. Qualifications required include operating various information technology systems, understanding and utilizing related publications, possessing distinct communicative and writing skills, and the ability to work independently and closely with additional logistical functional areas. The duties involve administration and operational procedures, office and warehouse management procedures, preparation and use of military publications and the preparation of accounting documents. Formal schooling is provided to Marines entering the Aviation Supply Specialist and Aviation Information Systems Specialist MOSs. Types of entry-level jobs include work as aviation supply logistics and AIS. There are a wide variety of billets available in the OccFld ranging from duty at all levels of the Marine Aircraft Wing/Marine Aviation Logistics Squadron to various Non-FMF billets such as HMX-1 and instructor duty. Aviation Logisticians are primarily aviation supply, aviation maintenance, aviation ordnance, and avionics personnel on higher headquarters staffs that coordinate/conduct aviation logistics planning in support of OPLANS/CONPLANS. In addition to a thorough understanding of their primary MOS, these personnel are involved with the Marine Aviation Logistics Support Program (MALSP), the Marine Corps Planning Process, the Joint operations Planning and Execution System (JOPES), Maritime Prepositioning Force (MPF) operations, and employment of the aviation logistics ship (TAVB). The Aviation Logistics OccFld has been expanded to include principal responsibility in the management and execution of CNO and CMC-directed strategies for continuous process improvement.

nlx_method: NLx employer-demand profiles; private-only ownership unverified. Six-digit profiles pool specialty weighted task incidences after the existing review exclusion mask and five-job task-support floor; destination SOCs require 200 postings and nonzero tasks. Military profiles use binary accepted task presence and the same NLx reference RCA weights as civilian profiles: reciprocal positive task shares (zero weight for reference-absent tasks) of pooled retained support-five NLx weighted incidences across 1,016 reference specialties (912 eligible comparison candidates), sqrt(q * rca_weight), then L2 normalization and cosine. No military crosswalk codes enter the task ranking. All positive top-20 results retained; zero-similarity destinations are not recommendations. Shared field/rating duties are included; general Naval Standards remain separate by paygrade. Summary compares non-future individual source entries (versions can repeat) with nonempty reference sets; grouped, future and general-standard entries remain in all outputs. Hit@k is the fraction with at least one reference SOC recovered; ties are averaged exactly. References outside NLx remain in denominators. DMDC reference status is from July 2024, not current 2026 status.
